issues: The only source's quote is the Finlex page title ('Henkilörekisterilaki | 471/1987 | Suomen säädöskokoelma'). It supports the name, the number and the year and nothing more. The finlex.fi page renders the statute text by script, so the fetched page is only a title and menu. The note's claims about the supervising Data Protection Ombudsman and about replacement in 1999 by a Personal Data Act implementing the EU Directive had no source.

All the claims are correct. The original statute text in Finlex's open-data service gives the signing line 'Helsingissä 30 päivänä huhtikuuta 1987' and entry into force on 1 January 1988, and it makes the tietosuojavaltuutettu the supervisor. The Personal Data Act 523/1999 expressly repeals 471/1987. The government bill HE 96/1998 says the new act would replace the 1987 law and align it with the EU Data Protection Directive. Primary sources for each were added, and the note now gives the exact dates.
The coordinates (60.1725, 24.9335) are Parliament House in Helsinki, which is correct.

fieldFixes.note: Finland's first general law on personal data files, given on 30 April 1987 and in force from 1 January 1988, with the Data Protection Ombudsman (tietosuojavaltuutettu) as supervisor. It was repealed in 1999 by the Personal Data Act (523/1999), which brought Finnish law into line with the EU Data Protection Directive.

issues: The note's second clause ('the Garante ... publishes it as part of its founding legislation') is vague and is not what the page says. The page is the Garante's docweb copy of Law 675/1996, consolidated with Legislative Decree 467/2001. The substantive point, which the page does support, is that the law itself created the authority: 'Art. 30. Istituzione del Garante' / 'E´ istituito il Garante per la protezione dei dati personali' [the Garante for the protection of personal data is established]. Footnote 49 shows that this paragraph was amended by Legislative Decree 123/1997, so the Garante's current name comes from that amendment.

Rewritten with facts from the same page: published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 5 on 8 January 1997, in force 120 days after publication (Art. 45), and repealed under Art. 183 of the Personal Data Protection Code (2003).

'Italy's first general data-protection law' matches the standard account. Italy had only sectoral rules before 1996, and the page does not contradict it. The coordinates (Montecitorio, Rome) are fine.

fieldFixes.note: Italy's first general data-protection law, dated 31 December 1996 and published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 8 January 1997; its Article 30 established the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali. It was repealed by the 2003 Personal Data Protection Code.

issues: 'Adopted 27 July 2006' is imprecise. The same Kremlin page says 'Принят Государственной Думой 8 июля 2006 года' [adopted by the State Duma on 8 July 2006] and 'Одобрен Советом Федерации 14 июля 2006 года' [approved by the Federation Council on 14 July 2006]. 27 July 2006 is the date the President signed it, which is the date the law carries.

The localisation paraphrase ('stored and processed in databases located in Russia') is too broad. Law 242-FZ requires operators to ensure 'запись, систематизацию, накопление, хранение, уточнение (обновление, изменение), извлечение' [recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification (updating, changing) and retrieval] of Russian citizens' personal data using databases in Russia, with exceptions. It does not localise all 'processing' (обработка). The same correction was made to the event russia-personal-data-localisation-law-2014 in global-2.

The 2014 amendment and its date of entry into force had no source on this record. The 152-FZ page lists 'от 21.07.2014 № 242-ФЗ' among its amending laws. Sources were added: the 242-FZ text, whose Art. 4 as amended by 526-FZ gives 1 September 2015, and DLA Piper's authority page for Roskomnadzor.
The coordinates (55.7575, 37.615) are the State Duma on Okhotny Ryad, which is fine.

fieldFixes.note: Signed on 27 July 2006, after passage by the State Duma on 8 July. Amended in 2014 by Law 242-FZ (in force 1 September 2015) to require operators to record, store, update and retrieve Russian citizens' personal data using databases located in Russia, with some exceptions.
